transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I'm here because I've been struggling with really severe, long-lasting mood swings that I just can't seem to control. For about a year and two months, I was dealing with a deeply depressed mood, but I've also had periods of extreme, overflowing energy and intense irritability that lasted for about 11 months.

During these periods of high energy, or even when your mood was stable, did you ever experience things like hearing voices, seeing things others couldn't, or having beliefs that others found highly unusual?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I've never heard voices or seen things that weren't actually there, and I didn't hold any unusual beliefs during those high-energy times or when my mood was stable.
During those times of high energy, did they cause major disruptions in your work or relationships, or even lead to hospitalization? Or were you still able to manage your daily life fairly well?

It definitely wasn't manageable and completely derailed my life, though I was never hospitalized. I'm really embarrassed to admit it, but I made reckless investments and spent huge amounts of money that caused my family severe financial distress. I also engaged in some risky behaviors that ended up ruining my relationships.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were Bipolar I Disorder and Bipolar II Disorder. The patient described a period of high energy and irritability lasting 11 months that caused severe impairment in functioning (reckless investments causing severe financial distress and risky behaviors ruining relationships). This level of impairment meets the criteria for a manic episode rather than a hypomanic episode, which rules out Bipolar II Disorder and confirms Bipolar I Disorder.
